questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"The Junagadh rock inscription of the Shaka ruler Rudradaman (second century CE) records the history of the Sudarshana lake: 'The lake, with well-joined water-gates and conduits... was originally built by the Vaishya Pushyagupta, the provincial governor of the Maurya King Chandragupta; a conduit was ordered to be made by the Yavanaraja Tushaspha for the Maurya King Ashoka... but in a terrible storm, the dams burst and a breach of 420 cubits occurred, emptying the lake. Rudradaman repaired the breach, making the embankment three times stronger, entirely out of his own private treasury, without oppressing the people of his country by exacting forced labour (vishti) or imposing taxes.' questionText: Which of the following statement is not true about mahajanapadas of the sixth-century BCE:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Validates both propositions as sound NCERT facts.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid scientific statements erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
The sixth century BCE is regarded as a major turning point in early Indian history, marked by the emergence of sixteen major territorial states called mahajanapadas. Buddhist and Jaina texts list sixteen states (such as Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, and Avanti). While most were monarchies ruled by rajas, some were oligarchies known as ganas or sanghas (like the Vajji sangha). Each had a fortified capital city, and rulers maintained standing armies and administrative bureaucracies. Stating that texts mention twenty states is factually incorrect.
Hence, option (A) is correct.

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Names) List-II (Associations)
(A) Piyadassi
(I) Script
(B) Kalinga
(II) Reporter
(C) Kharosthi
(III) Asoka
(D) Pativedaka (IV) Coastal Orissa
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Epigraphic terms: 'Piyadassi' (pleasant to behold) was the standard honorific title used by Emperor Asoka in his rock and pillar edicts (A-(III)). Kalinga was the ancient name for coastal Odisha conquered in Ashoka's eighth regnal year (B-(IV)). Kharosthi was the right-to-left script used for Ashokan edicts in the northwest (C-(I)). In Major Rock Edict VI, Ashoka commanded the 'pativedakas' (special reporters) to report public affairs to him at all times and places (D-(II)). Match: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
